misconceptions.description: Building the prototype screen or task first and then back-filling a claim, so the task drives the evidence model instead of the reverse
misconceptions.trigger: learner starts the matrix from the task column and invents a claim to justify a screen they already built
misconceptions.feedback: Start from the claim about what the learner should know or do, derive the observable evidence, then design the task. The task is last in the ECD chain.

misconceptions.description: Treating a fully populated traceability matrix as aligned without checking that each task actually elicits the evidence its row names
misconceptions.trigger: learner points to completed cells but never checks whether the task could produce the listed observable
misconceptions.feedback: A complete matrix is not an aligned matrix. Check each row: can this task produce exactly the evidence named, for this claim?

misconceptions.description: Writing a subjective impression in the evidence column instead of an observable learner behavior
misconceptions.trigger: evidence cell says learners will feel confident or find it useful rather than naming an action that can be recorded
misconceptions.feedback: The evidence cell must name something observable in the prototype, such as a selection, a sequence, or a constructed response, not a feeling.
